name: Gebr. Niemeijer
desc: French-style bakery with pastries, croissants, breads, sandwiches all baked fresh on premises. Open for breakfast and lunch, eat-in or takeaway. Bring the kids and eat in the small playroom upstairs.

name: Van der Linde
desc: Its officially a bakery, but they don't sell bread. They do sell Amsterdam's most famous whipped ice cream, lovely almond cookies and cakes. The texture is really creamy and soft, it melts easily and they put it in a con

name: Haring & Zo
desc: Serving for example fish sandwiches

name: Rob Wigboldus Fishmonger
desc: Herring sandwiches for €3.50.

name: Pasta Pasta
desc: Serves delicious pastas, made just as you want them. Choose a sauce, topping and pasta for a tasty, but well-priced meal.

name: Julia's
desc: Italian cuisine, both eat-in and take-out; notable take-out item: Penne Bolognese with a tasty vegetarian sauce instead of a meat sauce.

name: OCHA

name: Thaise Snackbar Bird
desc: Very crowded little snack bar with Thai food. Not to be confused with the restaurant of the same owner, on the other side of the street. Try the chicken in oyster sauce.

name: New King

name: Greetje
desc: Traditional Dutch, alongside French classics. Located in an historic building on a quiet side street near Central Station; it's off the beaten track so most of the diners are local. Open 6 days a week (not Mondays); a re

name: Kantjil & de Tijger
desc: Great spices and meat dishes, Indian/Indonesian food. Try the Nasi Goreng Rames.

name: Rembrandt Corner
desc: Around the corner of the "Rembrandt Huis" is a very nice "Eetcafe" with fresh food, WiFi hot spots and internet workplaces. Try the dish of the day or the mussels.

name: Tony's NY City Bagels

name: Amsterdam Jewel Cruises
desc: À la carte dining while cruising the canals.

name: Blue
desc: The selling point of this cafe is its 360 degrees view over Amsterdam. Its interior is minimalist and stylish. A great place to have a Dutch cup of coffee while taking in the views. Unfortunately, it's only open at dayti

name: De Jaren

name: Filter
desc: Small eco-friendly coffeebar situated in the lobby of hotel Ecomama. Serves great coffee, breakfast and a small selection of sweet and savoury treats. Also organic tea, juice and the best grilled-cheese sandwiches. Have

name: The Grasshopper
desc: On the edge of the Red Light District, has an upper-floor bar.

name: Hannekes Boom

name: Brouwerij de Prael
desc: A brewery, tasting room and beer shop all in one.

name: Cracked Kettle
desc: This beer, wine, and spirits shop carries independent, unique, and rare bottles. The staff are friendly, but the space is quite confined and obtaining bottles from the very top shelves requires assistance and a dust rag.

name: De Bierkoning
desc: Not a café, but a 'supermarket' specialized in beer. It has over a thousand beers, about half of it Dutch.

name: In De Wildeman
desc: A very well stocked beer café, or actually beer tasting room (bierproeflokaal) in the centre of the inner city. 17 beers (usually from various countries) and a cider on draught, and about 250 different bottled beers offe

name: Belgique
desc: One of the smallest bars in Amsterdam, there is seating for at most 15 people. Specialising in Belgian beers, extensive menu that includes some hard to find beers on tap. This place is smoke friendly so don't be surprise

name: Cuba
desc: Great bar, really nice atmosphere, close to the Red Light District with a nice terrace in the summer. Selection of cheap cocktails and long island ice tea.

name: Gollem
desc: A special beer café, serving many beers, especially from Belgium, Germany, Czech Republic and other countries.

name: Katoen
desc: Close to the southern part of the Canal District. Alternative music and cosy atmosphere also in the evenings.

name: Molly Malones Irish Pub
desc: Authentic Irish pub with food. Mix of expatriates, locals and tourists, friendly staff, on a canal off the Zeedijk, close to Centraal Station and Warmoesstraat. Open every night, live music in the week-ends and large-scr

name: Schuim
desc: The super comfy cafe is a great place to spend entire rainy days at a time. It heats up quite a bit at night. Pot smoking seems to be tolerated even though Schuim is definitely not a "coffeeshop".

name: Speijk
desc: Awesome bar with lost of fun, artsy crazy locals. Various DJ play different styles. Open till late in the morning. Best place to meet laid-back and awesome Amsterdammers!!

name: Bitterzoet
desc: This placed used to be alternative, but changed ownership and is now more hip hop and R&B oriented. Check their agenda to see what they're doing.

name: Winston Kingdom
desc: Music venue and nightclub in the red light district.

name: 420CAFE
desc: Known for their moderate prices. The music played here is Classic Rock & Frank Zappa.

name: Bluebird
desc: One of the best selections of pot in Amsterdam.

name: De Dampkring
desc: The shop was featured in a scene in Ocean's Twelve. Very decent hashish ("Rifman" products), rather high prices. Has won the Cannabis Cup numerous times.

name: Green House
desc: Usually pretty crowded but when warm or if you can get a seat definitely one of the nice coffeeshops near the Red Light District. Also has a bar next door.

name: Hill Street Blues
desc: Lively atmosphere but buy cannabis elsewhere.

name: Kadinsky
desc: It looks completely different from before, and now has three floors with a slick minimalist design.A great place to smoke your goods, and actually serves a good cup of coffee too.

name: Cafe Kadijk

name: De plantage
desc: Big restaurant with a nice terrace in the summer, open all day with breakfast, lunch and dinner.

name: Restaurant Plancius
desc: Has a nice high tea.

name: Tempura
desc: Nice Japanese restaurant, with a very lovely guest woman.

name: De Pizzabakkers
desc: Hip pizza restaurant, with good stone-baked pizzas. Suitable for children. Almost always busy, so reservation is recommended.

name: Aguada
desc: Indian and Indonesian influenced. Cosy restaurant. The rendang is a little too sweet but the thali is excellent.

name: Brouwerij 't IJ

name: Café Smit & Voogt
desc: Locals love this place. It is situated inside a beautiful building and has timber booths and seating inside . There is also seating on the footpath which is well placed to catch the afternoon sun. Serves a selection of b

name: Pancakes! Amsterdam

name: The Pancake Bakery
desc: Large selection of sweet or savory pancakes.

name: Frens Haringhandel
desc: A stall offering simple Dutch seafood fare like Kibbling (fried fish) and Haring (raw herring).

name: De Blauwe Hollander

name: Damsteeg
desc: They specialise in fish dishes, but they also have a wide variety of meat and vegetarian meals to choose from. With bar.

name: Letting
desc: Indian-owned breakfast, brunch and lunch spot. Letting offers a range of soups, sandwiches and scones, and it's on a street which is packed with an ever-changing line-up of fun boutiques.

name: Holtkamp
desc: Best pastry cafe in Amsterdam. Much better than the Zeitan, which many recommend. Do try the "holdkampf" with fillings! The Sachertorte is famous as a favorite of the former Queen Beatrix.

name: Alberto's Steakhouse
desc: Uruguayan Steakhouse with well-grilled steaks

name: Akbar
desc: Indian restaurant, Muslim (halal) / Hindu (no beef). Good quality dishes from different regions of India.

name: La Margarita
desc: This Caribbean restaurant offers a huge range of plates, including three different vegetarian options. Every dish comes with ample sides of white rice, black beans, plantains, and vegetables. In addition to having great

name: 't Arendsnest

name: Dan Murphy's
desc: One of the many Irish pubs in the city. People from all over the world meet here and watch football, rugby and typical Irish sports like hurling and Gaelic football while drinking a pint of Guinness.

name: Feijoa
desc: Cocktail bar with a lovely atmosphere, pleasant music and friendly staff, including one of the Netherlands leading cocktail barmen. Will make any cocktail you ask for.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
desc: This is close to, or right next to the Holland Casino also close to the Leidseplein. Great service, great food, and plenty of drinks.

name: Mulligans Irish Music Bar
desc: The oldest Irish bar in Amsterdam, Mulligans has live music most nights. This is where the traditional music crowd gathers.

name: l'Opera

name: Chicago Social Club
desc: Amsterdam's nightlife king Casper Reinders joined with the founders of Bitterzoet and the owners of Boom Chicago to bring quality clubbing to the Leidspelein.

name: Escape
desc: A large, fairly uninspiring nightclub that mostly plays mainstream house music. The first hall is large and attracts the more or less wannabe hip people of the city, although the crowd is diverse. The second hall upstair

name: Jimmy Woo
desc: The most glamorous club in Amsterdam offers a selection of house and R&B, with a spectacularly lit dance floor downstairs. It is relatively small and there is table service, so it feels a bit like a VIP room. Entry polic

name: Paradiso
desc: Sometimes referred to as a nightclub, it feels more like a nightly music venue and is the safest bet in town. Its interior is phenomenal as it is housed in a former church, but the main room has relatively bad acoustics.

name: Studio 80
desc: This is a somewhat more underground, intimate club that's easy to miss because of its flashy neighbours. It prides itself on trying to stay at the forefront of electronic music in the city.

name: Sugar Factory
desc: Bit of a remarkable place that integrates art, music, culture, theatre and nightclub into one. It has a relaxed atmosphere with an eccentric, artistic audience.

name: The Cave Rockclub
desc: Cozy metal bar with friendly bar staff and interesting regulars, with live performances by touring metal bands on weekends.

name: Waterhole
desc: Light rock/funk jam sessions in a dingy but atmospheric bar with pooltables. Live bands play every night of the week.

name: Betty Too
desc: Absolute gem, cozy and friendly place with moderate prizes and interesting, international crowd.

name: Bulldog
desc: This is the original shop that used to be a police department. Now it turned into a chain of touristy coffeeshops, bars, hotels and even an energy drink.

name: Global Chillage
desc: Good produce and nice tunes but uncomfortable seating.

name: Grey Area
desc: Tiny, but famous for their outstanding weed, especially "American" strains.

name: The Otherside
desc: Gay coffeeshop.

name: Burgermeester

name: Kinnaree
desc: Amazing Thai food. Good atmosphere, good service despite being quite busy, but the food is why you would come here. Highly recommended.

name: Long Pura
desc: Indonesian food, try the rice table.

name: Proeverij 274

name: Maloe Melo

name: 't Smalle
desc: Some say this place has the most beautiful terrace in Amsterdam. It's not big but you sit right beside the canal. And if it's too cold to sit outside check out the beautifully restored interior in this laid-back place.

name: Cafe P 96
desc: Great character at this pub, lovely outdoor terrace on a houseboat makes for a nice evening or afternoon. Good selection of Dutch and Belgian beers.

name: Soundgarden
desc: Top metal/grungy/punky pub, most relaxed drinking atmosphere in town. Really nice, secluded terrace for drinking beer in the sun. can smoke, but not buy, puff.

name: Bar Brandstof
desc: Relatively new bar with a big and often busy terrace. Gets absolutely crowded on Friday after work hours

name: Bar Struik
desc: Hangout for the urban 20 and 30-somethings. Every day except Friday they serve 1 dish for {{EUR

name: Cafe Chaos
desc: Typical Amsterdam brown bar. Throw your peanuts shells on the floor while looking at the furniture.

name: Barney's
desc: Coffeeshop.

name: Coffeeshop Ibiza
desc: Big coffee shop.

name: Albina
desc: It's cheap and very good. If you arrive around dinnertime you probably have to wait for a table. The surroundings are depressing but the food is so good you will come back anyway.

name: Tjin's Gelderlandplein
desc: Tasty, great value Surinamese take-out. Sandwiches. Located a short walk from the Zuidas area hotels. A few tables are also available to eat in.

name: CTaste
desc: Dining in the dark. All waiters are blind, and serve you dinner in a completely dark restaurant. A very weird, but actually quite fun experience.

name: FRNZY
desc: Small restaurant with indoor and street seating. Serves good noodle salads and sandwiches with a Vietnamese influence.

name: OCCII
desc: A rock venue for cutting-edge music (punk, noise, riot grrrl, etc.)

name: Club Media
desc: Completely organic menu, fair selection, good prices, lovely staff, free fruit!

name: Katsu
desc: Just around the corner from Media, good prices + nice atmosphere.

name: 't Blauwe Theehuis
desc: Basic bar and beer garden

name: De Roos
desc: Quite tea house with a small garden.

name: Dosa

name: Foodhallen
desc: International food court with 20 food-stands housed in a large building that was once a tram depot.

name: Hap Hmm
desc: Traditional Dutch cuisine. The restaurant may be cramped, but it does serve some quality and rustic Dutch fare. This place is cash only.

name: Sora Sapporo Ramen - West
desc: Small ramen restaurant with friendly staff, quick service, and good selection of ramen & appetizers. Also serve beer & sake. Closes early and small seating so might want to reserve on weekends.

name: TonTon Club West

name: Cafe L'Affice
desc: Small bar with friendly staff and a cosy and candle-lit atmosphere. Selection of beers on tap and in bottles, including a triple blonde specially made for the bar. Small selection of bar food as well.

name: Club 8
desc: A large alternative place with lots of art on its walls. There's ping pong, a very local and fairly young crowd.

name: Boerenjongens Eetwinkel
desc: A deli shop annex lunch room with products from the region.

name: IJsburg
desc: Ice cream shop.

name: Biertuin

name: Bloem op IJburg
desc: Italian restaurant.

name: Silk Road Restaurant
desc: Eastern and Western fusion meals with both à la carte and (on highly occupied days o­nly) a live cooking theme buffet. The restaurant has a view of the river IJ. Open 7 days per week for lunch and dinner.

name: Espressofabriek
desc: Coffee bar.

name: N.A.P.
desc: A harbour-side cafe and restaurant with a view of the marina. You can just stop by for a cup of coffee, have breakfast, lunch or dinner. Stylish interior.

name: Delirium Café Amsterdam
desc: With over 500 bottled beers and 20 craft beers on draft, the biggest craft beer bar in Amsterdam

name: Panama
desc: This nightclub is relatively close to the city centre. It has its fair share of nice nights and the view on the water is excellent.

name: Canvas

name: Café Modern B.V.
desc: A restaurant and cafe in a hall which used to be a bank.

name: Café-restaurant Stork
desc: A fish and seafood restaurant in an old factory on the banks of the river.

name: Hangar Amsterdam
desc: A redesigned aircraft hangar, turned restaurant.

name: Mount Everest Tandoori
desc: An Indian and Nepalese restaurant. Vegetarian friendly.

name: Pllek
desc: A bar and restaurant in an old industrial area, by the river.

name: Kam Yin Chinees Surinaams restaurant
desc: Surinamese and Indonesian cuisine. Very good Moksi Meti (marinated pork and sausages with noodles). Popular with the locals. Take-away.

name: Lebkov & Sons
desc: Sandwich bar. Mainly caters to office workers in surrounding buildings. Try the hummus & sun-dried tomato.

name: Lomnava Kenkey House
desc: One of the few Ghanaian snack bars in Amsterdam. Specializes in Kenkey (a sort of sourdough dumpling), but has a wide range of West-African cuisine at very reasonable prices.

name: Marmaris Grill & Pizza

name: Oma Ietje
desc: Inevitably, hipsters have even found their way into the Bijlmer. Part-funded by crowdfunding. Very worthy 'Swedish style' coffee house. Coffee, biological lemonade and cakes. Also showcases art by local artists.

name: Elixer

name: Yemayá’s Vegan Corner
desc: Surinamese Caribbean vegan food made by a local collective. Also delivers within Zuidoost and Diemen.

name: De Proefzaak

name: Kokusai
desc: Japanese/Chinese sushi, grill and wok restaurant near Amstelveen Stadshart shopping centre. All you can eat concept, à la carte possible during lunch and after 21:00.

name: Aan de Poel
desc: 2 Michelin stars restaurant

name: Buenos Aires
desc: Argentinian grill restaurant in the "old village".

name: Du Monde Bar & Kitchen
desc: Bar and restaurant in the "Old Village".

name: Feng Bistro
desc: Modern Asian cuisine inside an old windmill "De Dikkert".

name: Kaya
desc: Korean restaurant

name: Le Pain Quotidien
desc: As you might guess form the French name, they have bread based menu, but also offer bowls, soups, salads and quiches.

name: De Pizzabakkers Zaandam
desc: Italian pizza baked in the wood oven, prepared with fresh ingredients.

name: Blacksmith
desc: Small pub in the old workplace of a blacksmith. On the Hogedijk near the old harbour. A truly local pub with beer-tasting.

name: De Drie Noten
desc: A small bistro-style place with a limited menu and simple but tasty dishes for a good price. Dishes include entrecote with sauces and salad, chicken madras curry and monkfish with spicy tomato-sauce.

name: De Witte Swaen
desc: A pancake restaurant with some 60 different sweet and savory pancakes and the typical Dutch poffertjes (thick, mini-pancakes). However, if you'd rather eat something else, there's a range of salads, fish and meat dishes

name: De Kraai
desc: This is an excellent pancake house in an authentic former granary. Their specialty are Dutch pancakes, but they also have a range of cakes, salads, soups, snacks, and drinks.

name: Museum Cafe

name: Four Seasons
desc: Right in the centre of the village, this place serves modern Asian cuisine, with a touch of fusion cooking.

name: 't Waepen van Naang Nuan
desc: Tasty Thai food. On Fridays and Saturdays after 10.30pm, the music is turned up and this becomes a lounge bar serving Thai fingerfood.

name: De Waegh
desc: Located in the old weigh house, now a monumental building, this restaurant serves French/Mediterranean food. In summer, there's a lovely outdoor terrace along the water.

name: Het Weeshuis

desc: This restaurant, nicely located next to a windmill, is a nice place to just sip a cup of coffee. Full meals are also served, they have the usual Mediterranean fish and meat dishes, as well as Dutch pancakes. The staff ca

name: Pan & Koek
desc: Dutch pancake restaurant mostly aiming at families with children. They serve the usual pancakes, but also some original ones, such as pancakes with shawarma or Parmesan cheese.

name: Veensche Plas
desc: Its feature is its beautiful outside terrace, next to the water with a view over the rural landscape and the lakes. Their lunch consists of several bread dishes, while most dinner dishes are meat and fish in Mediterranea

name: Berestein

name: 't Swaentje

name: Dynasty
desc: Typical to-go Chinese/Indonesian restaurant which Dutch town offers. Don't expect a fancy restaurant, just good food for not too much. This place does offer spicy dishes from China's Sichuan province which is quite uncom

name: De Sloep
desc: It's generally a good restaurant, but even though they seem to want to be a top-class restaurant, it really doesn't qualify for that. It has a nice location at the water, but the service is a bit informal and feels a bit

name: Pronto
desc: Italian pizzas, spare-ribs and shawarma. Not much to say about this one, it's a simple budget place for a quick snack.

name: Solo
desc: Indonesian restaurant with cuisine from Central Java. The atmosphere is relaxed, but looks a bit old-fashioned (funnily it adds something to the experience). Try the "rijsttafel", it's the best dish they offer. Don't wor

name: Restaurant Het Drechthuis
desc: Restaurant for lunch and dinner near the Loosdrechtse Plassen with terrace view over the water. Do not expect luxury cuisine here, but the menu is extensive and is known for many fish and grill dishes.

name: De Schalkse
desc: Big terrace with a view on the river Vecht. And you can see the circular fort at Ossenmarkt.

name: Thai Faa Faet
desc: Outside the city; very good Thai food.

name: 't Weesperplein
desc: Very cosy interior. There are trees in the middle of the restaurant. Good service, high-quality food.

name: Alhambra
desc: Closed Monday. Terrace available with a view on the Kom.

name: El Mejor
desc: Terrace available with a view on the Kom.

name: Cafe 't Gat van Weesp
desc: Pooltable. Terrace available with a view on the river Vecht.

name: Cafe de Weespermop
desc: Little brown cafe with a pooltable. Terrace available with a view on the river Vecht.

name: Cafe De Natte Krant
desc: Little brown cafe. Terrace available with a view on the river Vecht.

name: Cafe 't Helletje
desc: Interior is very cosy with a big reading table in the centre. Terras available with a view on the river Vecht.

name: De Dames Van Amstel
desc: Pool table and reading table. Terrace available with a view on the canal Oude Gracht.

name: Toeters En Bellen
desc: Cafe for young people. Big sunny terras available with a view on the river Vecht and the Kom. Closed every Monday.

name: Weesper Taveerne
desc: Outside the centre. No terrace. Local people.

name: Burger King
desc: Not just your average Burger King, this is the busiest one in the world with 1.3 million visitors a year. It has never closed since its opening in 1993. But the menu is the still the same. Burgers.
